csv_project_name: VKB Offshore Feasibility & Prelim Shoreline Design Study
csv_scope_of_work: The Village of Key Biscayne ( Village ) pursuant to Florida Statutes 287.055, the Consultants Competitive Negotiation Act ( CCNA ), as may be amended, hereby issues this Request for Qualifications ( RFQ ) to interested and qualified firms to receive sealed proposals ( Proposals or Responses ) to develop a scientifically validated and implementable framework for hybrid offshore artificial reef systems that reduce shoreline erosion, enhance coastal resilience, and provide significant ecological co-benefits for the Village of Key Biscayne
csv_disciplines_requested: Civil Engineering, Geotechnical Engineering, Construction/Project Management, Feasibility Studies, Planning/Master Planning, Biological Studies/Natural Resources, Environmental Engineering/Planning/Design, Groundwater/Hydrogeology
csv_comments: '- Project Number: 2026-09- Contract Participation Goal: Prevailing Wage- Project Funding: NOAA/USACE/FDEP- Prevailing wage rates may apply.- Pre-Submittal Meeting: 06/01/2026 10:00 AM EDT- Pre-Submittal Location: Key Biscayne BZP Conference Room, Suite # 250 88 West McIntyre Street, Key Biscayne, Florida 33149- Pre-Submittal Attendance: Recommended- Solicitation documents available online.- Questions Deadline: Submit questions online by 06/04/2026 09:00 AM EDT - Multiple Contracts may be AwardedPre-Bid meeting June 1 at 10:00 AM EDT
title: VKB Offshore Feasibility & Preliminary Shoreline Design Study
short_description: Feasibility and preliminary design study for offshore reef systems improving shoreline resilience in Key Biscayne.
project_scope: Development of a scientifically validated and implementable framework for hybrid offshore artificial reef systems intended to reduce shoreline erosion, enhance coastal resilience, and provide ecological co-benefits for the Village of Key Biscayne. The notice indicates a feasibility and preliminary shoreline design study; no dimensions, lengths, areas, or other technical quantities are stated.
services: Civil engineering, geotechnical engineering, construction/project management, feasibility studies, planning/master planning, biological studies/natural resources, environmental engineering/planning/design, and groundwater/hydrogeology.
relevance_explanation:
- Primarily a feasibility, environmental, and shoreline resilience study rather than structural design.
- Focus is on offshore artificial reef systems and coastal/environmental planning, not bridges, buildings, roofs, or special load-bearing structures.
- Includes project management, biological, environmental, and hydrogeological services, which are outside sbp's core target profile.
- No clear structural engineering scope, span, building, or complex load-bearing system is described.
construction_cost_explanation: No construction budget is stated in the notice. The procurement is for a feasibility and preliminary design study only, with funding sources listed as NOAA/USACE/FDEP, but no cost basis for a realistic construction estimate is provided.
fee_explanation: No fee information is stated. As this is an RFQ for consulting and study services without a disclosed budget or fee schedule, no reliable sbp fee estimate can be derived from the notice.
references_qualifications: Interested and qualified firms under Florida CCNA; specific minimum reference requirements are not stated in the provided notice. Disciplines requested include civil, geotechnical, environmental, planning, biological/natural resources, groundwater/hydrogeology, and construction/project management.
contracting_authority: Village of Key Biscayne, 88 West McIntyre Street, Suite 250, Key Biscayne, Florida 33149, USA. Contact: Procurement. Phone: 305-365-7577. Email: procurement@keybiscayne.fl.gov. Website: https://www.demandstar.com/app/suppliers/bids/533486/details
notes: Project #864006; solicitation/project number 2026-09. RFQ issued pursuant to Florida Statutes 287.055 (CCNA). Pre-submittal meeting: 2026-06-01 10:00 AM EDT, attendance recommended. Questions deadline: 2026-06-04 09:00 AM EDT. Contract duration: 24 months. Multiple contracts may be awarded. Although categorized here as Special structures for lack of a better fixed option, the project is essentially a coastal/environmental feasibility study and is not a strong fit for sbp.
